proofs.proof_tex:
The upper bound follows immediately from the certificate and the minimax definition:
\[
\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}
\le\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}
[\widehat R_{\alpha,n}]
\le C\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
We prove the all-procedure lower bound directly. Put \(m=n/2\), let
\(C=P=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(I=Q=\{m+1,\ldots,n\}\), and set
\(v=n^{-1/2}\mathbf1_n\). Choose \(s_0\in[s_-,s_+]\), possible because
\(s_-\le s_+\), and let \(d=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\). Select orthonormal vectors
\[
w_j=2^{-1/2}(e_{m+2j-1}-e_{m+2j}),\qquad 1\le j\le d.
\]
They are supported on \(I\) and orthogonal to \(\mathbf1_I\). Fix
\(\lambda>0\), put
\[
\beta=\frac{\sqrt2\lambda\sigma}{s_0n},
\qquad
a=\{1-2d\beta^2\}^{1/2},
\]
and, for \(\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_d)\in\{-1,1\}^d\), define
\[
u_C^\epsilon=n^{-1/2}\mathbf1_C,
\qquad
u_I^\epsilon=a\,n^{-1/2}\mathbf1_I
+\beta\sum_{j=1}^d\epsilon_jw_j,
\qquad
L^\epsilon=s_0n\,u^\epsilon v^{\top},
\qquad
D^\epsilon=0.
\]
Orthogonality gives
\[
\|u^\epsilon\|_2^2
=\frac12+\frac{a^2}{2}+d\beta^2=1.
\]
Hence \(L^\epsilon\) has rank one and singular value \(s_0n\). Moreover,
\[
2\|u_C^\epsilon\|_2^2=1,
\qquad
2\|v_P\|_2^2=1,
\]
so both overlap Grams equal one and satisfy every \(\kappa\le1\). Since
\(\sqrt n\,\beta=O(n^{-1/2})\) and \(a\to1\),
\[
n\max_i|u_i^\epsilon|^2\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
n\max_t|v_t|^2=1
\]
uniformly in \(\epsilon\). The strict inequality \(\mu>1\) therefore gives incoherence for all sufficiently large \(n\). Treatment support is immediate from \(D^\epsilon=0\), so every
\(\vartheta^\epsilon=(L^\epsilon,D^\epsilon)\) belongs to \(\Theta_n\).

Only the observed block \(I\times P\) depends on \(\epsilon\). For
\[
H_j=w_j(v_P/\|v_P\|_2)^{\top},
\]
the matrices \(H_j\) are orthonormal in Frobenius inner product, and the Gaussian projections satisfy
\[
Z_j=\langle H_j,X_{IP}\rangle
=\lambda\sigma\epsilon_j+\sigma\xi_j,
\qquad
\xi_j\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
All remaining observed Gaussian coordinates are independent of \(\epsilon\). Under the uniform prior on the hypercube, the posterior bits therefore factor, and the optimal bit decision is
\(\operatorname{sign}(Z_j)\), with independent error probability
\[
p=\Phi(-\lambda)>0.
\]
For any possibly randomized decoder \(\widetilde\epsilon\), the posterior mass of a Hamming ball is maximized by centering it at the coordinatewise posterior mode. Consequently, for every \(0<\delta<p\),
\[
2^{-d}\sum_{\epsilon}
\Pr_\epsilon\{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)\le\delta d\}
\le\Pr\{\operatorname{Bin}(d,p)\le\delta d\}
\le\exp\{-2d(p-\delta)^2\}.
\]
The last inequality follows by applying the exponential Markov inequality to the product Bernoulli moment-generating function.

Now take an arbitrary \((\widehat L_n,R_n)\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\). From its center define \(\widetilde\epsilon_j\) by the sign of the coefficient along
\(w_j(v_Q/\|v_Q\|_2)^{\top}\), after subtracting the common component; break zero ties lexicographically. If this sign is wrong, that coefficient differs from its true value by at least \(\lambda\sigma\). Since Frobenius norm is bounded by nuclear norm,
\[
\|P_W(\widehat L_n-L^\epsilon)\|_*
\ge\lambda\sigma\sqrt{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)}.
\]
Put \(\delta=p/2\) and \(r_n=\lambda\sigma\sqrt{\delta d}\). Uniform honesty implies
\[
\Pr_\epsilon\{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)\le\delta d\}
\ge1-\alpha-\Pr_\epsilon\{R_n\ge r_n\}.
\]
Averaging this inequality over \(\epsilon\) and using the preceding binomial bound shows, for all sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
2^{-d}\sum_\epsilon\Pr_\epsilon\{R_n\ge r_n\}
\ge1-\alpha-e^{-dp^2/2}\ge\frac12.
\]
Thus some admissible \(\epsilon\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_\epsilon R_n\ge\frac{r_n}{2}
\ge c\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\Theta_n\), and then the infimum over every uniformly honest procedure, proves the lower bound. The construction uses only the observed-law family; the arbitrary treatment-effect component is fixed at zero and never conflated with the missing counterfactual.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. Its principal interior benchmark is the balanced rank-one L-mask frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\) for \(\mu>1\), established by an all-procedure lower bound and a total polynomial-time one-block certificate whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are controlled separately. Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} is the indispensable boundary companion: at \(\mu=\kappa=1\), the admissible factor signs are locally discrete, an honest polynomial-time radius is \(O(\sigma)\), and the unrestricted tangent modulus remains of order \(\sigma\sqrt n\). Thus neither the interior frontier nor a tangent-modulus lower comparison extends to that boundary. Matching the tangent modulus over arbitrary admissible interior wedges remains open. The diffuse-weight ATT interval is only a coverage-valid duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge with a computable spectral radius, an all-procedure interior benchmark, and an explicit account of the active-incoherence boundary where the usual tangent geometry ceases to describe the admissible class.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, and quantitative overlap Grams isolate a deterministic-wedge confidence problem with a genuine phase split: the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask has an interior regime \(\mu>1\) and a saturated boundary \(\mu=\kappa=1\).
project_justification.fill: For the balanced rank-one L-mask, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} proves the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) two-sided frontier only in the interior regime \(\mu>1\). Its total spectral certificate is audited term by term, including the homogeneous Taylor remainder and the large-gap fallback tail. Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} proves the boundary phase change: when \(\mu=\kappa=1\), a polynomial-time uniformly honest procedure has radius \(O(\sigma)\), while the unrestricted tangent modulus is at least \(\sigma\sqrt{2n}\), so that modulus cannot furnish a uniform minimax lower comparison. The overlap-aligned tangent-packing question remains open only for arbitrary admissible interior wedges.

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential construction: their four-block SVD estimator has non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply a testing reduction for honest nuclear confidence diameter, but their experiment is isotropic Gaussian trace regression and their central obstruction is rank adaptation. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals and phase transitions for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block; their loss and procedure-specific target differ from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan provide debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions but report no global honest matrix radius. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the \(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} shows that at \(\mu=\kappa=1\) the honest radius can be \(O(\sigma)\) even though the unrestricted tangent modulus is order \(\sigma\sqrt n\); neither comparison should be read across that boundary. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng are functional-specific benchmarks for weighted effects; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem distinguishes collective low-rank uncertainty from the order-\(n\) radius obtained by summing entrywise intervals in the strict-incoherence interior \(\mu>1\); Theorem \ref{thm:general-wedge-boundary-obstruction} records the different \(\mu=\kappa=1\) boundary behavior.
statement_notes.gap: Yan and Wainwright prove sharp scalar widths, and Capponi and Stojnic characterize Frobenius residuals of one algorithm; neither gives an all-procedure tuple-indexed honest nuclear-radius frontier in the \(\mu>1\) interior or isolates why that frontier cannot be extended to the saturated \(\mu=\kappa=1\) boundary.
statement_notes.consumer: Researchers can report a simultaneous uncertainty set for the entire treated counterfactual block at the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) scale in the stated \(\mu>1\) benchmark, while using the boundary companion rather than extrapolating this rate to \(\mu=1\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(n=2m\), and abbreviate the unique balanced chart by
\[
 C=\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad I=\{m+1,\ldots,2m\},\qquad
 P=\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad Q=\{m+1,\ldots,2m\}.
\]
The balanced-mask and one-chart assumptions imply
\(W_n=I\times Q\) and
\(\Omega_n=(C\times P)\mathbin{\sqcup}(I\times P)\mathbin{\sqcup}(C\times Q)\),
so \(|\Omega_n|=3m^2\).

We first evaluate the consequences of the boundary value \(\mu=1\).  For any
\(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n\), the rank-one and strong-factor assumptions
give a singular-value decomposition
\[
 L_n=s_nu_nv_n^{\top},\qquad
 \lVert u_n\rVert_2=\lVert v_n\rVert_2=1,qquad
 s_-n\le s_n\le s_+n.
\]
The incoherence assumption at \(\mu=1\) gives
\[
 |u_{n,i}|^2\le \frac1n\quad(1\le i\le n),
 \qquad
 |v_{n,t}|^2\le \frac1n\quad(1\le t\le n).
\]
Each collection of squared coordinates sums to one.  Hence every one of the
\(n\) displayed inequalities is an equality.  There are therefore signs
\(p_i,q_t\in\{-1,1\}\) and a number
\(\ell_n=s_n/n\in[s_-,s_+]\) such that
\[
 u_{n,i}=\frac{p_i}{\sqrt n},\qquad
 v_{n,t}=\frac{q_t}{\sqrt n},\qquad
 L_{n,it}=\ell_np_iq_t.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{n}{|C|}u_{n,C}^{\top}u_{n,C}
 =\frac{n}{m}\frac{m}{n}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac{n}{|P|}v_{n,P}^{\top}v_{n,P}
 =\frac{n}{m}\frac{m}{n}=1,                                \tag{2}
\]
so the overlap-Gram condition at \(\kappa=1\) is compatible with, and is
attained by, every matrix in (1).

We next lower-bound the geometric quantity.  The class is nonempty: take
\(u_n=v_n=n^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_n\), \(s_n=s_-n\), and \(D_n=0\).
This tuple has exact rank one, satisfies the strong-factor bounds because
\(0<s_-\le s_+\), satisfies incoherence and overlap by (2), and satisfies the
treatment-support condition.  Fix this tuple, let \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_n)^{\top}\),
and choose a vector \(h\in\mathbb R^n\) supported on \(I\).  Then
\[
 \Delta=hq^{\top}=(\sqrt n\,h)v_n^{\top}\in\mathcal T_n(L_n)               \tag{3}
\]
by the definition of the rank-manifold tangent space.  Since \(h\) vanishes
on \(C\), the two coordinate projections in the definition of the wedge
modulus obey
\[
 \lVert P_{\Omega_n}\Delta\rVert_F
 =\lVert h_Iq_P^{\top}\rVert_F
 =\lVert h\rVert_2\sqrt m,
 \qquad
 \lVert P_{W_n}\Delta\rVert_*
 =\lVert h_Iq_Q^{\top}\rVert_*
 =\lVert h\rVert_2\sqrt m.                                  \tag{4}
\]
The last equality uses the identity
\(\lVert ab^{\top}\rVert_*=\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert b\rVert_2\)
for a rank-one matrix, which follows directly because its only nonzero
singular value is \(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert b\rVert_2\).
Choose \(h\) so that
\(\lVert h\rVert_2\sqrt m=\sigma\sqrt{2n}\).  Since \(r=1\) and
\(N_n=T_n=n\), (3)--(4) make \(\Delta\) feasible in the defining supremum for
\(\omega_n(L_n,\Omega_n)\), with objective value \(\sigma\sqrt{2n}\).
Consequently, by the definition of \(\mathfrak R_n\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n\ge \omega_n(L_n,\Omega_n)\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}.                \tag{5}
\]

It remains to construct a uniformly honest procedure whose radius is much
smaller.  Fix deterministic reference indices \(i_0\in C\) and \(t_0\in P\),
and set \(\operatorname{sign}(0)=1\).  All coordinates in the following sums
belong to \(\Omega_n\), so the definitions use only \(X_n\):
\[
 \widehat p_i=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sum_{t\in P}X_{n,it}X_{n,i_0t}\right)
 \quad(1\le i\le n),
 \qquad
 \widehat q_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sum_{i\in C}X_{n,it}X_{n,it_0}\right)
 \quad(1\le t\le n).                                        \tag{6}
\]
We give a uniform error bound for these signs.  Consider first \(i\ne i_0\).
By treatment support and the definition of the observed experiment,
\(X_{n,it}=L_{n,it}+E_{n,it}\) on \(\Omega_n\).  After multiplying the first
sum in (6) by \(p_ip_{i_0}\), its distribution is
\[
 S_i=\sum_{t=1}^{m}(\ell_n+\varepsilon_t)(\ell_n+\delta_t)
 =m\ell_n^2+G_i+H_i,                                        \tag{7}
\]
where the Gaussian-cell assumption implies that the pairs
\((\varepsilon_t,\delta_t)\) are independent over \(t\), their two entries
are independent, and every entry is \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\).  Here
\[
 G_i=\ell_n\sum_{t=1}^{m}(\varepsilon_t+\delta_t)
 \sim\mathcal N(0,2m\ell_n^2\sigma^2),
 \qquad
 H_i=\sum_{t=1}^{m}\varepsilon_t\delta_t.                    \tag{8}
\]
The elementary Gaussian Chernoff calculation
\(\Pr\{Z\le-x\}\le\exp\{-x^2/(2v)\}\) for
\(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,v)\) yields
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{G_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right\}
 \le \exp\!\left\{-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{16\sigma^2}\right\}.               \tag{9}
\]
For \(0<t<\sigma^{-2}\), direct integration of the two independent Gaussian
densities gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp(-t\varepsilon_t\delta_t)
 =(1-\sigma^4t^2)^{-1/2}.                                   \tag{10}
\]
If \(0<t\le(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\), then
\(-\tfrac12\log(1-\sigma^4t^2)\le\sigma^4t^2\).  Markov's
inequality, (10), and independence over \(t\) therefore give
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{H_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right\}
 \le \exp\!\left\{-\frac{mt\ell_n^2}{2}+m\sigma^4t^2\right\}.           \tag{11}
\]
Taking
\(t=\min\{\ell_n^2/(4\sigma^4),(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\}\) in (11) gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{H_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right\}
 \le \exp\{-m c_2\},
 \qquad
 c_2=\min\!\left\{\frac{s_-^4}{16\sigma^4},\frac14\right\}>0.          \tag{12}
\]
Indeed, the exponent is at most \(-m\ell_n^4/(16\sigma^4)\) in the first
case and at most \(-m/4\) in the second.  Equations (7), (9), and (12) show
that
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat p_i\ne p_ip_{i_0}\}
 \le e^{-mc_1}+e^{-mc_2},
 \qquad c_1=\frac{s_-^2}{16\sigma^2}>0.                      \tag{13}
\]
For \(i=i_0\), the sum of squares in (6) is positive almost surely, and the
claimed relative sign equals one.  Applying exactly the same calculation to
the column sum in (6), now using its \(m\) independent pairs indexed by
\(i\in C\), proves (13) with \(\widehat q_t\) and \(q_tq_{t_0}\) in place of
\(\widehat p_i\) and \(p_ip_{i_0}\).  A union bound, which does not require
independence between the different comparisons sharing a reference row or
column, thus gives, for
\[
 \mathcal S_n=\{\widehat p_i=p_ip_{i_0}\ \text{for every }i,
 \ \widehat q_t=q_tq_{t_0}\ \text{for every }t\},
\]
the uniform estimate
\[
 \sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}(\mathcal S_n^c)
 \le 4n\exp\{-m c_\star\},
 \qquad c_\star=\min\{c_1,c_2\}>0.                          \tag{14}
\]

Let \(\Phi\) be the standard-normal distribution function and define
\(q_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/4)\).  Complete the matrix by
\[
 \widehat\ell_n=\frac1{|\Omega_n|}
 \sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_n}X_{n,it}\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
 \qquad
 \widehat L_{n,it}=\widehat\ell_n\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
 \qquad
 R_n=q_\alpha\sigma\frac{m}{\sqrt{|\Omega_n|}}
 =\frac{q_\alpha}{\sqrt3}\sigma.                            \tag{15}
\]
This pair is measurable in \(X_n\), hence also in the randomization variables
allowed by the definition of \(\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\), and \(R_n\ge0\).
On \(\mathcal S_n\), put \(c=p_{i_0}q_{t_0}\).  Then
\(\widehat p_i\widehat q_t=cp_iq_t\), and (1) and (15) imply
\[
 \widehat\ell_n
 =c\ell_n+cZ_n,
 \qquad
 Z_n=\frac1{|\Omega_n|}
 \sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_n}p_iq_tE_{n,it}
 \sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{\sigma^2}{|\Omega_n|}\right).             \tag{16}
\]
It follows on \(\mathcal S_n\) that
\[
 P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)=Z_n p_Iq_Q^{\top},
 \qquad
 \lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*=m|Z_n|.            \tag{17}
\]
By the definition of \(q_\alpha\),
\[
 \mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\!\left(m|Z_n|>R_n\right)=\frac\alpha2.          \tag{18}
\]
Choose an even \(n_0\) so large that
\(4n e^{-(n/2)c_\star}\le\alpha/2\) for every even \(n\ge n_0\).
Combining (14), (17), and (18) by a union bound, without asserting any
independence between \(\mathcal S_n\) and \(Z_n\), gives uniformly over
\(\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n\)
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}
 \!\left\{\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*\le R_n\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha.                                                \tag{19}
\]
Thus (15) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\) for all even \(n\ge n_0\).
Its row correlations, column correlations, signed average, and outer-product
completion use \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic operations.  Since its radius is
deterministic, the definition of the minimax expected radius and (15) yield
\[
 0\le\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}
 \le\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}[R_n]
 =\frac{q_\alpha}{\sqrt3}\sigma=O(\sigma).                  \tag{20}
\]
Finally, (5) and (20) imply
\[
 0\le\frac{\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}}{\mathfrak R_n}
 \le\frac{q_\alpha}{\sqrt{6n}}\longrightarrow0.             \tag{21}
\]
Therefore a universal positive constant lower comparison
\(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\ge c\mathfrak R_n\) cannot hold over every
admissible parameter choice and wedge.  Equations (1) and (3) identify the
mechanism: at the active boundary \(\mu=1\), admissible singular vectors have
only coordinatewise sign choices, while the unrestricted tangent space still
contains every continuous direction \(hq^{\top}\) used in (3).
